misconceptions.description: Drawing population-level effectiveness or statistical-significance claims from a handful of moderated usability sessions
misconceptions.trigger: learner reports that a five-person test shows the design improves learning or beats the old version with confidence
misconceptions.feedback: Small-N moderated testing supports usability and design-failure claims, not efficacy. Scope the claim to observed friction in this sample.

misconceptions.description: Recording what testers did but never linking each observation to a specific design change and recheck
misconceptions.trigger: learner lists behaviors or scores but the trace shows no observation-to-revision pairing
misconceptions.feedback: Pair each meaningful observation with the design change it triggered and a plan to recheck it. The trace is the link, not the list.

misconceptions.description: Treating a one-of-five occurrence as either a confirmed defect or a percentage of the whole population
misconceptions.trigger: learner converts a single tester's struggle into a population rate or an immediate redesign
misconceptions.feedback: Record low-frequency signals as uncertain and watch for recurrence before committing a redesign or reporting a rate.
